section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that fear of G-d, unlike love, comes primarily through human effort, and therefore the request "Hashem our G-d be with us" emphasizes His assistance to our own work.
section.t: And one may add,
that the reason the term "treasury" is said specifically regarding fear,
even though this matter
(that the Holy One, blessed be He, needs, so to speak, man)
applies to all mitzvos,
for in order for the fulfillment of mitzvos to be as required, it is through love of Hashem or through fear of Hashem13,
and among the distinctions between love and fear is14,
that love of Hashem comes through a revelation of light from above,
and fear of Hashem comes
(primarily)
through the work of man.
And analogous to fear of a human king,
that the reason the people of the country fear the king is because they accepted him to be king over them15,
for the acceptance of kingship is through the people,
"You shall surely set a king over you"16.
And based on this, one can explain the phrase "May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our forefathers,"
for in fear of Hashem
(which is the beginning of service and its essence and root17),
the main thing is the work of man,
and the revelation of light from above
(Hashem our G-d)
is only an assistance to man,
"with us."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that fear, being total self-nullification like that of a servant, must come specifically through man's own acceptance of servitude, not through an external revelation.
section.t: Now, the reason for this, that fear comes primarily through the work of man,
one may say,
is because fear is self-nullification.
And particularly the fear of a king,
"You shall surely set a king over you, so that his awe shall be upon you"18,
that the self-nullification of this fear is connected with the fact that he is a servant of the king
[for the nature of a servant is that the awe and fear of the master is upon him],
that the self-nullification of a servant is total self-nullification,
and therefore it comes specifically through man,
for the action that is done in man through a revelation of light from above is like something additional to him,
and therefore the change that occurs in him through this is only in his mental conception,
but not a change in the man himself,
and in order to come to total self-nullification,
the self-nullification of a servant
[for the difference between a free man and a servant is in the very essence of his existence],
it is through man himself accepting upon himself to be a servant of the king.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that self-sacrifice, being total nullification, also comes primarily from man himself, so the request "May Hashem our G-d be with us" was fitting for the Rebbe's talk about self-sacrifice.
section.t: And one may say that the same applies to self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh),
for since self-sacrifice is total self-nullification,
and particularly when the self-sacrifice is for matters that according to law
(a command from above)
one is not obligated to give his life for them19,
therefore it is
(primarily)
not through a revelation of light from above, but through man giving his life.
And based on this, it will be understood even more that the request and prayer of the Baal HaGeulah
(in the sicha of 3 Tammuz)
was in the language of the verse "May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our forefathers,"
for he spoke then about the matter of the service of self-sacrifice,
and in this very matter, regarding many matters that according to law one is not obligated to give his life for, which come
(primarily)
from man himself,
and since in the service of self-sacrifice the main thing is the work of man,
and the revelation of light from above assists the work of man,
therefore he began his request and prayer
(in the language of the verse)
"May Hashem our G-d be with us."
